newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar heads lower as expiry looms.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar heads lower as expiry looms.

text.p: London's spot white sugar contract headed lower in the little time remaining before expiry as the March/May spread continued to narrow before close of business, traders said on Thursday.
One trade house was said to be a larger-scale bidder of the spread at the lower levels, while another was an active seller and causing it to contract further.
But scale-down buyers were also lurking under the market to pick up bargains, traders said.

"There's not much around...but anything could happen, the switch has come in a bit," said one, adding that the expected volume of physical delivery against the expired contract could total as much as three cargoes.
Origins are expected to be the European Union and possibly Poland.
At 1720 GMT March was down $1.90 at $303.00 and May down 30 cents at $301.20. Volume was much lighter than in recent sessions and totalled 1,847 lots.

Technically, the second-month May contract, about to take over the limelight of spot position, continued to trade above a bear trendline dating from the September high, while moving along a three-week upward channel.
Paris futures also moved lower and movements were tight. May was down 30 cents at $301.20 and August down by the same amount at $301.70.
